# Visavantajātaka (Ja 69)

**ID:** Ja 69
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**Title (Pali):** Visavantajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Visavantajātaka* (Ja 69) is a narrative belonging to the *Jātaka* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka. Set at Jetavana, the story of the present relates an episode concerning the Buddha's chief disciple, Sāriputta [Fausböll 1877]. After unintentionally eating a share of meal-cakes or wheat-cakes (*piṭṭhakhajjaka*) left for other monks, or being teased for overindulgence, Sāriputta scrupulously took a vow never to eat meal-cakes again [Appleton 2010; Lamotte 1944; Migot 1954]. To demonstrate that Sāriputta had possessed similarly uncompromising determination in past lives, the Buddha recounted a tale of a poisonous snake [Appleton 2010; Lamotte 1944].

In the story of the past, a physician summoned to treat a snakebite captured the offending snake and demanded that it suck the poison back out of the victim's wound or else face death by fire [Appleton 2010; Salguero 2017; Lamotte 1944]. Refusing to retract what it had once released, the snake chose death over taking back its vomited poison [Appleton 2010; Salguero 2017]. The central canonical verse opens with *Dhiratthu taṁ visaṁ vantaṁ* ("Curse that vomited poison") [Fausböll 1877; Salguero 2017]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the steadfast snake was Sāriputta, while the physician was the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1877]. Michael Slouber observes that the title *Visavanta* is a pun playing on *visam vantam* ("vomited poison") and *visavant* ("venomous" or "possessing venom") [Salguero 2017].

 Étienne Lamotte identifies an analogous apologue highlighting Śāriputra's unalterable resolve preserved in the Chinese translation of the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya (T 1421, fascicle 29) [Lamotte 1944]. DharmaNexus identifies no Pali-internal or cross-language matches meeting its threshold [DharmaNexus].
